fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK display at an arterial pedestrian crossing is a substantive final-design-stage safety issue: delayed driver detection directly threatens stopping for crossing pedestrians.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-001 provides a verbatim site-specific quote ('Drivers may be confused by competing background visual elements at night' at Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave) that directly supports the pivotal conspicuity-confusion claim.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no normative_basis_note, keeping the conspicuity/safety question distinct from any MUTCD compliance assertion.
justifications.recommendation_quality: 'Install a reflective border around the HAWK signal' is a specific, actionable, viable countermeasure (retroreflective signal-head/backplate bordering is an established conspicuity treatment), not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the exposed VRUs—are explicitly identified as road users and the scenario links late/misread driver detection to their protection during crossings.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance timing adequate for slower walkers at the corridor's highest pedestrian/bicycle collision frequency HAWK sites is a genuine, scheme-relevant safety issue at final design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim ('may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') is directly supported by the verbatim EV-US-016 quote, with site specificity anchored to the recorded case-study issue for these exact locations.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern (verify walking-speed assumptions) rather than a MUTCD compliance query, keeping the categories distinct within FHWA final-design audit semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (all six named sites), actionable (retiming/reprogramming), and viable via standard reduced assumed walking speed practice; only minor gap is no stated target speed value.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are the explicit focus: pedestrians and elderly pedestrians named as affected road users, with the evidence quote and scenario centering elderly walker exposure.
